Revenue may include players acquired before the selected period. The rough ratio does not measure a customer cohort over its lifetime. Acquisition costs are not available in the files. LTV is shown only for rows containing one original segment. Combined rows have no LTV forecast. Months with data counts distinct months with any reported revenue, not full coverage across every constituent segment.

How are the sources joined and metrics calculated?

Sources: Revenue is Commission in Dollar from the Comm file. Gross Revenue and Commission Performance are empty. FTD used for player-value calculations comes exclusively from the FTD file. The FTD column in Comm is shown separately as ftd-c for comparison only. ftd2ftd is FTD minus ftd-c.

Joining: Each source is first aggregated by Brand-Pl-Pr-CC and calendar month, then joined. Key matching normalizes whitespace and letter case. Main Brand, Main Platform, Product and Country Code come exclusively from Comm. If an FTD key exists in Comm in another month, its dimensions are taken from that key, while the FTD remains in its original month. Keys absent from Comm remain unassigned. #N/A keys are never joined to one another.

Rough ratio: Total revenue for the segment and period ÷ total assigned FTD for the same segment and period. Negative revenue is retained. The 23 suspected duplicate extra rows have not been removed. No ratio is calculated without FTD. This is not CAC: customer acquisition costs are not available in the files.

LTV model: A separate model is fitted for each original segment. Combined rows have no LTV forecast: Cₜ = a × Σ(rᵏ × Nₜ₋ₖ) + b × rᵗ. N is monthly FTD. a estimates first-month commission; r is the revenue persistence factor; b estimates revenue at the start of the window from earlier customers. a and b are nonnegative. Values of r from 0 to 0.995 are evaluated in steps of 0.005 using least squares. LTV = a / (1 − r). This is an extrapolation without discounting or costs, not a value observed at the individual customer level.

Assumptions: Missing FTD records are treated as zero while the assumption is enabled. Missing revenue rows are not treated as zero observations when fitting the model. The model assumes a stable declining revenue pattern, including the legacy-customer component. Changes in commission rates, customer mix, seasonality or payment delays may change the estimate. r is not an observed customer retention rate.

Forecast validation: The last six months are held out from the initial fit. Revenue is predicted conditional on the actual FTD recorded in those months. Error is calculated as Σ|predicted − actual| / Σ|actual|. This is compared with a simple forecast using the mean of the six preceding available revenue observations. After validation, the model is refitted over the entire selected period.

Estimate screening rules: At least 24 reported revenue months (18 before the test window and 4 within it), at least 50 FTD across at least 6 positive months, and sufficient FTD variation. Test error must be at most 50% and no more than 5% worse than the mean-based forecast. Estimates are withheld if r is at least 0.99, the sensitivity range spans more than a factor of 3 or includes zero, or the full-fit LTV differs by more than a factor of 2 from the initial fit. These are analytical screening rules, not a guarantee of accuracy or reliability.

Sensitivity range: The range of LTV values among models with fitting error no more than 10% above the minimum. This is not a statistical confidence interval and does not capture every risk in the model assumptions.
